current.summary: Roof terrace of about 2.5 × 4 m off the kitchen, terracotta tile floor, marble threshold step at the new doors. House wall: patched in several different renders around the doors, heavy black mould staining below the scalloped (tile-edge) parapet, a surface conduit running the full width, an outdoor socket box and festoon lights. To the left of the doors, a recessed alcove under a small tiled canopy holds the Vaillant gas boiler — not yet connected — with loose wiring, a yellow gas hose, an old brown stove and a gas cylinder stored in front. A satellite dish is fixed above. Beyond the alcove, under torn blue and green tarpaulins, is the outdoor kitchen: a timber unit with a tiled roof, with barbecues. Behind it, the view to the church and clock tower. The seating corner is formed by a tall rendered wall, mould-stained, and a rough stone wall with old louvred shutters hung on it and a small wooden hatch. Furniture: pallet seating with navy cushions, wooden table, wrought-iron bench.
keep: Rough stone wall with the hung shutters — belongs to the neighbour: do not render, paint or fix into it
issues: JOB 1 — Outdoor kitchen (under the tarpaulins): design and rebuild — image to come from ChatGPT
JOB 2 — Render and paint the walls that belong to the house, smooth and professional
JOB 3 — Make a door for the boiler alcove so the boiler is hidden
JOB 4 — Finish installing the boiler: connect gas and thermostat

target.concept: Smooth, warm-white rendered walls on the house side, the stone wall left rough as the feature, the boiler out of sight behind a louvred door painted to match, cables and conduit hidden, and a proper outdoor kitchen where the tarpaulins are now.

palette.name: Warm white (exterior)
palette.code: match to Farrow & Ball Lime White No. 1
palette.notes: Breathable and mould-resistant; avoid plastic acrylic masonry paint on these walls

palette.name: Boiler door — undecided
palette.notes: Recommendation: paint it the wall colour so it disappears. Alternatives: oak-tone to match the kitchen doors, or olive green

furniture.name: Boiler alcove door

furniture.name: Outdoor kitchen
furniture.detail: To design from the ChatGPT image: worktop, barbecue position, storage, weather cover

lighting.name: Festoon lights re-hung on a tensioned wire after painting

target.renderPrompt:
Edit this photo of a room in our house. Keep the exact camera angle and keep all the architecture exactly as it is — walls, room shape, windows, doors, beams, floor and fixed fittings. Do not add, move or remove anything structural, and do not change the furniture unless I say so below. Remove all clutter: tools, boxes, bags, dust sheets, loose cables, packaging, laundry and toiletries. Show the room finished and tidy.

Changes to make:
- Keep the terracotta tile floor, the view over the roofs to the church and clock tower, and the rough stone wall with the old wooden shutters hung on it — do not paint or change the stone wall.
- Remove the blue and green tarpaulins. In their place, under the same small tiled roof, a built outdoor kitchen: a rendered warm-white base, a thick wood or stone worktop, a built-in charcoal barbecue and a gas grill, shelves underneath for wood and pans.
- The house walls are smooth render painted warm white, with no stains, patches or surface cables.
- The boiler alcove is closed by a neat louvred door painted the same warm white.
- Festoon lights hung neatly on a taut wire. A few terracotta pots with a lemon tree, rosemary and jasmine.
- Keep the seating and table simple and tidy. Golden-hour light.

Style: photorealistic interior photograph, natural light plus warm 2700K lamps, no people, no text or labels.

scope: Render and paint the house-side walls

surfaces.prep: Take down festoon lights; electrician to chase the surface conduit and socket into the wall or re-route. Wash with a fungicidal/biocide treatment and leave to work; hack off loose and hollow render; repair; then a full-face mesh-reinforced base coat so the different old patches do not show through.
surfaces.finish: Fine smooth finishing coat, then 2 coats breathable silicate/siloxane exterior paint
surfaces.notes: The mould sits under the parapet: water is running down the face. Fix the cause first — check the top of the wall/parapet and add a drip edge or capping, or the stain will return through new paint

surfaces.prep: Neighbour's wall — not ours. Do not render, paint or drill. Protect during works.

Boiler first: a registered gas installer connects the gas with fixed pipework (no loose hose), the flue and the thermostat, tests it and issues the declaration of conformity. Then tidy wiring into trunking and render the alcove inside.
surfaces.finish: Louvred door across the opening, painted
surfaces.colour: To decide — recommendation: same warm white as the walls, so the door disappears
surfaces.notes: The door MUST be ventilated and must not restrict the flue — follow the boiler manual's clearances. Do not store the gas cylinder or stove in the alcove.

notes: Order: boiler connection → conduit/cables hidden → render → paint → boiler door → outdoor kitchen → lights back up
Render in mild dry weather — not in frost or strong sun
brief.access: Through the kitchen — protect the kitchen floor
